# linux_file (Resource)

Manages a file: its content, permissions and ownership. The file is replaced atomically, so readers never see it half written.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_file" "nginx_site" {
  path  = "/etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf"
  mode  = "0644"
  owner = "root"
  group = "root"

  content = templatefile("${path.module}/app.conf.tftpl", {
    server_name = "app.example.com"
  })
}

# Binary content.
resource "linux_file" "logo" {
  path           = "/var/www/app/logo.png"
  content_base64 = filebase64("${path.module}/logo.png")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `path` (String) Absolute path of the file.

### Optional

- `content` (String) Content of the file, as UTF-8 text. Conflicts with `content_base64`.
- `content_base64` (String) Content of the file, base64-encoded, for binary files. Conflicts with `content`.
- `create_parents` (Boolean) Create missing parent directories. They are not removed with the file. Defaults to `true`.
- `group` (String) Group, as a group name or GID. Defaults to the primary group of the user running the commands.
- `mode` (String) Permissions, in octal. Defaults to `0644`.
- `owner` (String) Owner, as a user name or UID. Defaults to the user running the commands.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Path of the file.
- `sha256` (String) SHA-256 digest of the content, hex-encoded. Known at plan time: use it to restart a service when the file changes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the path of the file.
terraform import linux_file.nginx_site /etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf
```
